title: The Pace Car
clue: Your dog drives, you keep up, and the pit stops are the whole point.
reveal: You jog or stride a flat loop and your dog sets the speed. Four pit stops, picked by your dog's nose, get a line each in a pit-crew report. Then your dog picks the finish spot, and a trophy toy appears there. You are the pace car; the throttle is theirs.
objective: Run or stride a flat loop at the speed your dog chooses, stop at four pit stops, let your dog pick the finish spot and find the trophy toy there.
instructions: Pick a flat loop with soft footing (dirt path, grass track, quiet park lane) away from traffic, in cool, dry hours. Choose four pit stops you can name: bench, gate, big tree, water tap. Pack a favorite toy as the trophy, a harness, six-foot leash, water, bowl, waste bags and a pocket notebook.
Start with a relaxed walk. Check the ground with the back of your hand: skip hot, icy or sharp surfaces. Note the leash rules for the path.

Rev up: say 'ready' and pick up to a jog only if your dog moves into a trot on their own. You are the pace car: you match them, never the other way round. If the leash tightens, you slow down. Never tug or speed up to keep them going.

Pit stops: at each landmark, drop to a walk, stop and let your dog sniff for a full minute while you offer water. Jot one line for the pit report ('Stop 2, the bench: extremely interesting, 40 seconds of nose').
Traffic rules: when you meet other dogs, bikes or runners, drop to a walk, move aside and keep the leash slack. No dashing past anyone.
Your dog can switch to a walk, sit down or head for the nearest shade whenever they like. A walked lap counts exactly the same: the pace car simply walks.

Checkered flag: walk the last stretch slowly and let your dog choose the finish spot, a patch of shade or soft grass they like. When they settle there, bring out the trophy toy from your bag and let them have it. Offer water and sit a while, read the pit-crew report out loud, then check paws and between the toes.
twist: Your dog is the driver and you are only the pace car: they set the speed, name the pit stops with their nose and choose the finish spot, where a trophy toy is revealed.
variations: Walking version: stride briskly instead of jogging and keep the same four pit stops.
Hot-day version: go early or late, shorten the loop to two pit stops and finish in the shade.
Owner who cannot jog: roll or walk the loop with the dog trotting alongside only if they choose to, and skip the speed-up step.
Small dog: halve the stretch between pit stops and let them trot at their own rhythm.
completion: It counts once you have reached one pit stop at your dog's pace, written one line in the report and let your dog pick a finish spot. A walk-only lap counts in full.
photoIdea: Your dog at a pit stop, nose down, with the landmark behind them, from the side at their level.
memoryPrompt: Which pit stop held your dog longest, and where did they decide to trot?
supplies: Notebook or phone for the pit report
safety: Cool, dry hours only. Check the ground with the back of your hand and skip hot sidewalk.
The dog sets the speed: never tug or speed up, and slow to a walk if they lag or pant hard.
Jog only on soft, level ground. Skip it for dogs with joint trouble.

keepsake.headline: THE PACE CAR
keepsake.explainer: I set the pace today. My human just kept up

teaser: A race with no rivals, a leader who loves it and a trophy at the finish line.
